I will do it close to how I have done before, and only change a little where it helps. On 5.5 mu, I cannot gamble much. I have farmed a long time, so I look first at what gave a steady harvest, what the neighbors around me use, and what I can afford. Cotton eats fertilizer and needs more spraying, but if I keep water and pest control on time, it still gives me cash. Stevia also needs feeding and clean field management, and with my well water I can keep it from suffering in dry spells. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than lose yield, so I will not cut too hard on nitrogen or potash. I will use improved seed where I have seen it work locally, plough the land at the start, water several times through the hot months, and keep pesticide timing tight on cotton because once insects get ahead, it costs more to chase them.
